transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've come in today because I've been feeling extremely energetic and barely needing any sleep for the past few weeks, which has been really intense. On top of that, I've been hearing voices and constantly feeling like people are watching me. It's all getting a bit overwhelming, so I wanted to get some help.
Do you experience these voices or feelings of being watched even when you are not feeling this intense energy or lack of sleep?

Yes, I do. Even during times when my energy is completely normal and I'm sleeping fine, those voices and the feeling of being watched are still there. It seems like those scary experiences can happen completely on their own, separate from the high-energy phases.

Over the course of your illness, have there been significant periods lasting at least two weeks where you experienced these voices and paranoia without having any notable mood swings or changes in your energy levels?

Yes, absolutely. There have been times lasting at least two or three weeks where my mood was completely stable and normal, but the voices and the feeling of being watched were still there. During those periods, I didn't feel any of that high energy or any depression at all.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type), Schizophrenia]. The patient's report that psychotic symptoms persist for weeks in the absence of any mood symptoms (manic or depressive) satisfies the DSM-5-TR criteria for Schizophrenia and specifically rules out Schizoaffective Disorder, which requires that mood symptoms be present for the majority of the total duration of the illness.
